title: transparent-error-propagation-and-tenant-backoff-adapter
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Customers are seeing intermittent ambiguous 5xx responses combined with client-side timeouts and large numbers of duplicate retries during tenant surge events. Symptoms include: non-deterministic 502/503/504 spikes, request duplication observed in backend logs, and request traces that terminate at the edge without a clear upstream error. This ticket drives a cross-stack fix: (1) make error propagation transparent so clients get actionable signals (429/503 with retry-after where appropriate), (2) add a tenant-level backoff adapter at the edge to prevent retry amplification, and (3) enforce optional idempotency tokens and per-tenant socket quotas to reduce duplicate load and connection exhaustion.
investigation_notes:
- Initial tracing showed many requests with identical payloads lacking idempotency keys; retries were being replayed to the serving fleet.
- Edge proxy was returning 502/504 in several cases where upstream timed out; client SDKs treated these as retryable and reissued requests quickly.
- Connection pool exhaustion observed per-tenant on gateway nodes; TCP TIME_WAIT and keepalive exhaustion correlated with surge windows.
- Some 5xx responses lacked structured error codes in the payload, making it impossible for caller to distinguish transient overload vs terminal model error.
- Hypothesis: combination of missing idempotency, aggressive SDK retry defaults, and edge mapping of upstream timeouts into generic 5xx leads to retry storms and elevated tail latency.
decision_log:
- Add a deterministic mapping at the edge that returns 429 with Retry-After for overload-detected cases instead of 5xx when upstream signals congestion.
- Implement a lightweight tenant backoff adapter that tracks recent failures and enforces exponential backoff per tenant with jitter.
- Require SDKs to send optional Idempotency-Key header for non-streaming generation calls; server will honor if present and dedupe within a short window.
- Introduce a soft per-tenant socket/admission quota on gateway nodes to prevent single-tenant connection floods from starving others.
- Rollout behind feature flag with metrics-driven ramp.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy edge error mapping and tenant backoff as feature-flagged binary to canary cluster (5% of traffic) + keep legacy behavior for remaining traffic. 2) Run A/B with metrics: 5xx rate, 429 rate, request duplication count, p95 latency. 3) If duplication drops >= 60% and customer visible errors drop >= 40%, expand to 25% then 50% over 48-72 hours. 4) Enable SDK idempotency header guidance and default in next SDK patch. 5) Gradually enable socket quotas with conservative limits and per-tenant overrides for Dedicated/private tiers.
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback (disable feature flag) if: 1) overall success rate drops by >5% for top 10 tenants, OR 2) p99 latency increases >30% sustained for 30m, OR 3) any customer reports functional regression in acceptance test suite. Rollback steps: flip feature flag at edge, reconfigure backoff state store to passthrough mode, notify customers via status page and account teams.
timeline_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket opened after customer X reported repeated timeouts and duplicate charges; on-call ran initial triage.
2026-02-22: Added tracing hooks to edge and gateway to capture idempotency headers and socket usage; confirmed lack of idempotency keys in many failing traces.
2026-02-24: PoC of tenant backoff adapter validated in staging; duplicate request count reduced in simulation by ~70%.
2026-02-27: Design review with PM and Security; decided to keep idempotency header optional but recommended. Security signoff for telemetry changes required minimal data retention.
2026-03-01: Canary deploy scheduled for feature-flag rollout tomorrow morning; engineering rota assigned for 48h burn-in.
notes_for_support: If customer experiences immediate regressions, record tenant id and time window and escalate to ENG-913579 channel. Provide customers with temporary mitigation: reduce client retry aggressiveness or enable SDK opt-out for edge backoff if they require immediate bypass.
